results.title: Best AI code review tools for monorepos
results.content:
The challenge: in a monorepo, a change to a shared library can break several applications without that showing up anywhere in the pull request, and different projects in the same repo usually need their own rules.
 Kodus: best for teams that need to standardize code review across different projects. Offers custom rules per directory, contextual analysis, BYOK and self-hosting, making it a fit for organizations that care about governance.
 Greptile: best for monorepos with complex dependencies. Builds a graph of the repository to analyze relationships between files, functions and shared components.
 CodeRabbit: best for teams with a high volume of pull requests. Offers incremental reviews, path instructions and architectural impact analysis. [...] Kody Rules inherit across three levels, Global, Repository and Directory. Global rules flow down to every project, while specific rules and exclusions let teams tune the review criteria where it matters.
 When a pull request touches two or more directories that each have their own setup, Kodus falls back to the repository’s configuration instead of arbitrarily picking just one directory’s rules.
 Teams can set a different model or provider per repository or directory, so a more sensitive project can run on a stronger model, with token cost billed straight by the provider when the team uses BYOK.
 Memories let a team bank instructions and technical decisions for future reviews, without turning every piece of institutional knowledge into a formal rule. [...] #### Why Greptile makes sense for monorepos

In a monorepo, different projects often share general conventions while still needing their own rules. Greptile’s hierarchical setup lets a team park standards at the repository root and let child directories inherit that guidance automatically.

When a rule doesn’t fit a particular project, it can be switched off by ID without losing every other inherited instruction, so a team isn’t duplicating an entire rule set just to carve out one exception.

Greptile also leans on codebase context to work out how implementations relate to each other. On changes touching shared libraries, that helps surface problems beyond the lines that actually changed.
